Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In this directed weighted graph implemented via an adjacency list, the cost of the operation for vertex v is the number of outgoing edges from v (i.e., the out-degree of v), and the total cost of the entire sequence of |V| operations equals the sum of all out-degrees, which is exactly |E|. The worst case for a single operation arises when one vertex is connected by outgoing edges to as many other vertices as the graph structure permits.

* (a) The cost of the worst possible single operation is **|V| − 1**, which occurs when a single vertex has directed outgoing edges to every other vertex in the graph (the maximum out-degree in a simple directed graph).
* (b) The average amortized cost based on aggregate analysis is **|E| / |V|**, because the total cost over all |V| operations is |E| (the sum of all out-degrees equals the total number of edges), and dividing by the number of operations gives |E| / |V| per operation.
